speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the onset, duration, and specific nature of your double vision, and tell me if you experience any numbness or tingling in your limbs.

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, ESR, CK, and Thyroid Function Tests.
REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies and Anti-MuSK Antibodies.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The initial tests for infection, muscle inflammation, and myasthenia gravis have returned normal. To further investigate your double vision and upper limb weakness, do you experience any difficulty with chewing or swallowing?

REQUEST TEST: Brain MRI with contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The initial inflammatory and neuromuscular tests were normal, and I have requested a Brain MRI to evaluate for a central cause. While we await those images, do you notice any drooping of your eyelids or slurred speech when you look up or down?

REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI_contrast.

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis (Diagnosis based on characteristic fatigability of ocular and limb muscles despite normal standard screening and antibody tests, prompting a re-evaluation of specific antibody assays or a clinical trial of pyridostigmine).
